detail.what_it_is: An AI-native operations workspace for small businesses, where each business outcome - virtual staging a listing, turning food photos into menu images, a product video, a logo, a headshot, a Daily Digest of local opportunities - is its own guided workflow over an asynchronous Firebase Cloud Functions and Cloud Tasks generation pipeline, on the stated premise that owners should not have to learn AI to put it to work.
detail.what_it_does: attainDesk turns common small-business needs into guided, business-specific AI workflows from one workspace: create social-media content; virtually stage real-estate listings; turn property images into video tours; create short promotional product videos; transform ordinary food photos into polished menu and marketing images; generate business logos; create professional headshots; generate branded meeting backgrounds; and a Daily Digest that surfaces relevant market developments, local business groups, events and opportunities. The named verticals are real estate, food, manufacturing, construction, education, clothing and professional services. The features differ and the goal is stated as one: help a small business understand its market, present itself professionally, reach customers and grow without needing a large specialist team.
detail.how_they_tested: Nothing is measured in the sense this catalog counts as measurement. There is no test suite, no eval, no accuracy, acceptance or rejection-rate figure, and no quality claim for any of the nine workflows - no statement, for instance, of how often a generated virtual-staged room or product video is acceptable to the business that asked for it. What the page offers instead is usage: 'early customer usage has been important in helping us make those decisions' between impressive-sounding and genuinely valuable features, which is product research rather than a test result, and 13 businesses as the population it was gathered from, unpublished per workflow. The one appearance of the word testing is in the description of how the code was written - Gemini-powered coding agents and Antigravity used for 'architecture brainstorming, coding, testing, debugging and iteration' - so the assertion is that testing happened, with no harness, count or result attached and no repository to read it from. The absence is load-bearing for a claim of this shape: the acceptance rate of a generated marketing image is the number a buyer of this product would need.
detail.limits_they_disclosed: Three, and all three are stated as product restraint rather than technical failure. The first is 'avoiding the temptation to simply put powerful AI models behind generic prompt boxes' - owners want an outcome, so the workflows are organised around what the business is trying to accomplish, with most prompting and model complexity abstracted behind the experience. The second is workload heterogeneity: text, image, video and research jobs differ by orders of magnitude in cost, some completing quickly while others are computationally intensive and asynchronous, and the Cloud Tasks plus Firebase layer is what keeps that invisible to the user. The third is described as a continual judgement call between features that are technically impressive and features that create genuine value, with early customer usage cited as the thing that decided it.

detail.what_it_is: An AI education platform that sells outputs instead of lessons — automated workflows, a published book, a dashboard, a deployable system — pitched at people who hear about AI daily and have never used it, with no measurement of any kind on the page.
detail.what_it_does: Described as a practical AI execution platform for individuals, small businesses, educators and organisations, combining AI education, workflow automation, practical system building, AI-assisted content production and operational training. The focus areas it lists are AI workflow design, no-code and low-code automation, AI writing and publishing, productivity systems and agent utilisation; the promised learner outputs are automated workflows, published books, AI-generated media, operational dashboards and deployable business systems. What a session on the platform actually looks like — a course, a template library, a hosted workspace, a marketplace of workflows — is not distinguished anywhere on the page.
detail.how_they_tested: No evaluation of any kind is described: no learner outcomes, no completion or retention rate, no before/after time measurement, no pilot with a named organisation, and no test suite. The effectiveness claims and the 'save measurable time' principle would normally be where a training product puts its evidence, and neither is present.
detail.limits_they_disclosed: Two, both framed as design tensions rather than things the build resolved: simplifying AI for non-technical users who are overwhelmed by APIs, automation tools, coding environments, model selection and a changing ecosystem; and balancing accessibility, scalability and real technical depth, since too simple means no meaningful solutions and too technical means beginners stop. The stated remedy is that they continuously refined the curriculum and workflows to reduce friction while preserving capability, with no example of a decision made or a threshold chosen.
detail.worth_note: The genre is crowded and this entry is indistinguishable from it: practical application rather than theory, a list of output types, a stated tension between too simple and too technical. What would move it off this label is a single number from a real cohort, and the page itself names which number — people learn faster when they can automate something useful, publish a real result or save measurable time. The record is held for the absence of the measurement it argues for, not for the aim, which is a good one.

detail.what_it_is: Same product, later write-up: a screenwriter drags a file, picks from candidates, and never types a prompt.
detail.what_it_does: She drags the file on; ninety seconds later she sees 37 scenes, 6 characters, and the sentence 'this chapter is 12 shots, it'll cost $4.50, about half will come out right first time'. She picks a style (the buttons carry the difficulty delta), casts from candidate portraits at $0.02 each, then presses one button and reviews each rendered shot with keep/again. Output is one file with subtitles burned in, in one of three languages. Casting is a hard gate: no shot generates until every character in it has an approved reference. A Gemini model watches each finished clip for observable facts (people in frame vs people called for, text creeping in) and the findings sit on the shot card; on 'again' the rejected take and its findings are written to the ledger first, and the retry prompt carries them. When a line trips the content filter they generate the shot anyway and move the line into the subtitle layer, so no word of her script changes. Every prompt exports as text, markdown or JSON.
detail.how_they_tested: A seeded ×0.92 bias in the ledger to prove the calibration view fires; per-shot outcome logging; no published test suite.
detail.limits_they_disclosed: During testing a deliberate ×0.92 bias was seeded into the ledger to check that the calibration view would catch it; the account of what the check was for is the most concrete engineering-culture signal on either page.
